summary: Acadia National Park lookout on Sargent Mountain: CCC-built wooden cabin on a stone base, 1941; removed about 1949-50; a 2014 blog post describes scattered remains.

facts.design: wooden cabin on a stone base, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps
facts.status_note: Removed around 1949-1950; a 2014 blog post describes only scattered remains on the site

events.note: Built by the CCC as a wooden cabin on a stone base, about 1,000 feet due north of the summit
NPS says it existed until 1949 and was soon after removed; Forest Lookouts gives c.1950; the blog says operations might have ended the following year

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NPS says the lookout existed until 1949 and was soon after removed; Forest Lookouts gives c.1950; the Memorials of Acadia blog says operations might have ended the following year. The story gives both.
Forest Lookouts lists Acadia National Park. NPS says the cabin was part of the Maine Forestry Service's fire lookout network. The record keeps Acadia National Park as agency.

notes_for_editor: Removal date varies by source (1949 NPS, c.1950 Forest Lookouts). Agency wording differs: Forest Lookouts and the brief say Acadia National Park; NPS says the lookouts were part of the Maine Forestry Service network. The Memorials blog gives a coordinate for the lookout about 350 m north of the brief's point, which is probably the summit, so the brief coordinate may be the summit rather than the cabin. No photo with a clear licence was found. No source describes the site today beyond the 2014 blog's scattered remains.
